function.name: calculate_electric_current
function.description: Calculate the electric current through a conductor given voltage and resistance. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

voltage.description: The voltage across the conductor in Volts. This is a float type value.

resistance.description: The resistance of the conductor in Ohms. This is a float type value.

conductance.description: The conductance of the conductor in Siemens. Optional if resistance is provided. Default: 0.3 This is a float type value.

message.content: Electricity wasn’t “discovered” by a single person; it was gradually uncovered by many scientists over centuries. Early observations date back to Thales of Miletus (circa 600 BCE), who noted static electricity from rubbing amber. In the 16th–17th centuries William Gilbert coined the term *electricus* and studied magnetism and static electricity. The 18th‑century experiments of Benjamin Franklin (e.g., his kite experiment) helped establish the nature of electrical charge. Later, Alessandro Volta invented the voltaic pile (the first battery) in 1800, and Michael Faraday’s work on electromagnetic induction in the 1830s laid the groundwork for modern electrical engineering. Thus, the discovery of electricity is the result of cumulative contributions from many thinkers rather than a single individual.
